A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UMoE. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered hyperparameter tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling experiments, zero-shot evaluations, ablations, and attention analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measured training throughput and inference latency in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The architecture and attention formulations are retained. Figure 3 now explicitly implements the shared and low-rank query projections already defined by Equation 11 in v1. The balancing-loss disclosure and discussion of possible MLA/SwiGLU extensions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu, Wikitext-103, the same eight downstream tasks, and the same attention-analysis examples. The added timing evaluation does not introduce a new dataset or substantive task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Dense, FFN-MoE, MoA, and SwitchHead. The new timing table evaluates the same model set, calling the dense baseline GPT. Newly cited Universal Transformers and MoEUT are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces a timing protocol measuring 1024-token prefill latency and training throughput on a single NVIDIA H100. Existing language-modeling and downstream evaluation settings are retained, including the unchanged hyperparameter tables.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a targeted efficiency analysis examining whether similar theoretical MAC counts translate into comparable measured runtime at both model scales. Existing sharing, allocation, activation, pre/post-mixing, and attention-specialization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 states that the timing results in Table 9 are averaged over multiple runs, without specifying counts, seeds, or uncertainty estimates. The new checklist also explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting for pretraining.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation results, and plotted findings are retained. New Table 9 adds timing results: base UMoE reports 0.2197-second prefill latency and 71,461 tokens/s throughput; large UMoE reports 0.4392 seconds and 9,194 tokens/s. These are additional measurements, not improvements over corresponding v1 results.

T1.justification: The attention derivations, low-rank query equation, FFN-as-identity-attention interpretation, and complexity expressions in Table 8 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified attention/FFN experts, parameter sharing, and competitive or superior predictive performance. Cross-layer parameter sharing is added only as future work.

C2.justification: v2 discusses GQA incompatibility and possible MLA/SwiGLU extensions, attributes practical runtime overhead to routing and sparse execution, and explicitly acknowledges missing mathematics/code evaluation and unexplored reasoning scaling. Existing interpretations of expert specialization remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the Switch Transformer load-balancing loss, documents roughly one week of base-model pretraining, specifies the new timing setup, and makes Figure 3 consistent with Equation 11. The checklist adds dataset-license information. Existing hyperparameter values and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Universal Transformers and MoEUT references when proposing future parameter sharing across Transformer layers. It also discusses GQA and MLA compatibility. The central related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. Changes include replacing token-embedding terminology with hidden-state terminology in the method description, repairing cross-references, and adding efficiency and limitations subsections plus the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adds the runtime table and revises Figure 3's pseudocode display. Existing figures and hyperparameter tables are relocated or renumbered, with limited table-header and pagination changes. The underlying diagrams, attention heatmaps, and retained result plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies practical timing evidence missing from v1: Table 9 reports large UMoE latency of 0.4392 seconds versus 0.2950 seconds for the dense baseline. Together with corrected pseudocode and explicit evaluation limits, this improves transparency. The gain remains limited because timing uncertainty is unspecified and Section 4.2 still describes MAC ratios as slowdown without reconciling the larger measured latency gap.
